## [New release of LLM adds support for reasoning traces, OpenAI Responses, server-side tools, and smarter logging](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/4/new-release-of-llm/#atom-everything)
*Simon Willison's Blog* | 04/08/2026 | Score: 1.00
Tags: api_update, mcp, product_launch, github_release, developer_tool, cli_tool, tool_update, agent_tool

> <p>I released <a href="https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/changelog.html#v0-32">LLM 0.32</a> this morning, the most significant new version of LLM since the initial launch of the project. The new version includes support for visible reasoning traces, server-side provider tools, redesigned content-addressable SQLite logs, new models, and new features enabled by the OpenAI Responses API. I also released a new version of the <a href="https://github.com/simonw/llm-anthropic">llm-anthropic plugin</a> with substantial updates of its own.</p> <h4 id="headline-features-for-llm-cli-users">Headline features for LLM CLI users</h4> <p>Running LLM against reasoning models now <strong>displays their reasoning traces</strong> to standard error, so you can see what they are "thinking" without that information being included in the standard output that you might pipe to another tool. Add <code>-R/--hide-reasoning</code> to turn this off.</p> <p><img src="https://static.simonwillison.net/static/2026/best-pelicans.gif" alt="Running llm "think about the best thing about pelicans" in the macOS terminal window - grey text outputs saying Exploring pelican qualities, then after a paragraph of that a white paragraph of text comes out saying: The best thing about pelicans is their wonderfully oversized, practical design: that enormous bill and pouch look comical, but they make pelicans remarkably skilled fishers. Even better, many species cooperate—working together to herd fish before scooping them up. They’re a great mix of goofy, graceful, and surprisingly clever." style="max-width: 100%;" /></p> <p>LLM includes support out-of-the-box for the <strong>GPT-5.6 model family</strong>, and the new default model used with <code>llm "prompt"</code> is now the inexpensive but capable <strong>GPT-5.6 Luna</strong>.</p> <p>LLM calls can now use <strong>server-side tools</strong> from various providers. OpenAI provide <a href="https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/openai-models.html#code-interpreter">a code execution environment</a> as a server-side tool; LLM can now run prompts that benefit from that like so:</p> <div class="highlight highlight-source-shell"><pre>llm --tool CodeInterpreter <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>Show current python and SQLite versions<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span></pre></div> <p>OpenAI also gets a <a href="https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/openai-models.html#web-search">WebSearch</a> tool.</p> <p>The <a href="https://github.com/simonw/llm-anthropic">llm-anthropic</a> plugin adds <a href="https://github.com/simonw/llm-anthropic/blob/0.26/README.md#web-search">WebSearch</a>, <a href="https://github.com/simonw/llm-anthropic/blob/0.26/README.md#web-fetch">WebFetch</a>, <a href="https://github.com/simonw/llm-anthropic/blob/0.26/README.md#code-execution">CodeExecution</a>, and <a href="https://github.com/simonw/llm-anthropic/blob/0.26/README.md#mcp-connector">AnthropicMCP</a>, which looks like this:</p> <div class="highlight highlight-source-shell"><pre>llm -m claude-sonnet-5 -T <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>AnthropicMCP("https://datasette.simonwillison.net/-/mcp")<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> \ <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>how many rows in the blog_blogmark table?<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span></pre></div> <p>That causes Anthropic to execute MCP calls against my new <a href="https://simonwillison.net/2026/Jul/31/stateless-mcp/#datasette-mcp">datasette-mcp</a> plugin as part of a single request/response interaction with their API.</p> <p>The new <strong>llm openai endpoint</strong> command provides a tool for <a href="https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/other-models.html#run-against-an-endpoint-without-configuring-it">executing prompts against <em>any</em> OpenAI compatible endpoint</a> as a one-liner. These aren't logged, which makes this a handy tool for running one-off prompts against anything that speaks the lingua franca of the LLM API world.</p> <p>Here's how I use that to run prompts against Gemma 4 12B running in my localhost <a href="https://lmstudio.ai">LM Studio</a> API, via <code>uvx</code> (no LLM installation required) and mixing in the <a href="https://github.com/simonw/llm-tools-quickjs">llm-tools-quickjs</a> tool plugin for good measure:</p> <div class="highlight highlight-source-shell"><pre>uvx --with llm-tools-quickjs \ llm openai endpoint http://localhost:1234/v1 -m google/gemma-4-12b \ -T QuickJS <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>Use QuickJS to multiply 3434 * 2434<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> --td</pre></div> <p><img src="https://static.simonwillison.net/static/2026/openai-endpoint-gemma.webp" alt="Output reads Tool call: QuickJS_execute_javascript({'javascript': '3434 * 2434'}) 8358356 The result of 3434 * 2434 is 8,358,356." style="max-width: 100%;" /></p> <h4 id="new-features-in-the-python-api">New features in the Python API</h4> <p>LLM's Python API previously required you to create a conversation and then send messages to it one at a time. This was an abstraction over the true nature of LLMs, where each request carries a complete history of the messages that came before it. That abstraction started to get in the way for some more advanced cases, so the new release introduces a <code>model.prompt(messages=[])</code> parameter that can be used like this:</p> <pre><span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-s1">llm</span> <span class="pl-k">from</span> <span class="pl-s1">llm</span> <span class="pl-k">import</span> <span class="pl-s1">user</span>, <span class="pl-s1">assistant</span>, <span class="pl-s1">system</span> <span class="pl-s1">model</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">llm</span>.<span class="pl-c1">get_model</span>(<span class="pl-s">"gpt-5.6-luna"</span>) <span class="pl-s1">response</span> <span class="pl-c1">=</span> <span class="pl-s1">model</span>.<span class="pl-c1">prompt</span>(<span class="pl-s1">messages</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span>[ <span class="pl-en">system</span>(<span class="pl-s">"You are a helpful pirate."</span>), <span class="pl-en">user</span>(<span class="pl-s">"What is the capital of France?"</span>), <span class="pl-en">assistant</span>(<span class="pl-s">"Paris, matey."</span>), <span class="pl-en">user</span>(<span class="pl-s">"And Germany?"</span>), ]) <span class="pl-en">print</span>(<span class="pl-s1">response</span>.<span class="pl-c1">text</span>())</pre> <p>LLM previously returned an iterable sequence of strings from each prompt. This worked great when models returned a string response, but failed to predict the weird shape that models would evolve towards. Today many models return a mix of reasoning text, output strings, tool calls, and even image attachments. With LLM 0.32 you can <a href="https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/python-api.html#structured-messages-and-streaming-events">do this instead</a>:</p> <pre><span class="pl-k">for</span> <span class="pl-s1">event</span> <span class="pl-c1">in</span> <span class="pl-s1">model</span>.<span class="pl-c1">prompt</span>(<span class="pl-s">"Explain cats"</span>).<span class="pl-c1">stream_events</span>(): <span class="pl-k">if</span> <span class="pl-s1">event</span>.<span class="pl-c1">type</span> <span class="pl-c1">==</span> <span class="pl-s">"reasoning"</span>: <span class="pl-en">print</span>(<span class="pl-s">f"[thinking] <span class="pl-s1"><span class="pl-kos">{</span><span class="pl-s1">event</span>.<span class="pl-c1">chunk</span><span class="pl-kos">}</span></span>"</span>, <span class="pl-s1">end</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">""</span>, <span class="pl-s1">flush</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-c1">True</span>) <span class="pl-k">elif</span> <span class="pl-s1">event</span>.<span class="pl-c1">type</span> <span class="pl-c1">==</span> <span class="pl-s">"text"</span>: <span class="pl-en">print</span>(<span class="pl-s1">event</span>.<span class="pl-c1">chunk</span>, <span class="pl-s1">end</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-s">""</span>, <span class="pl-s1">flush</span><span class="pl-c1">=</span><span class="pl-c1">True</span>) <span class="pl-k">else</span>: <span class="pl-en">print</span>(<span class="pl-s">f"Other event: <span class="pl-s1"><span class="pl-kos">{</span><span class="pl-s1">event</span><span class="pl-kos">}</span></span>"</span>)</pre> <p>Combine these features and we can <em>finally</em> provide a robust implementation of the semi-standard OpenAI chat completions API, which I've now released as the <a href="https://github.com/simonw/llm-chat-completions-server">llm-chat-completions-server</a> plugin:</p> <div class="highlight highlight-source-shell"><pre>llm install llm-chat-completions-server llm chat-completions-server --port 9000 <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Server is now running on http://127.0.0.1:9000/v1</span></pre></div> <p>Now you can run prompts against LLM via that server, using the new <code>llm openai endpoint</code> command!</p> <div class="highlight highlight-source-shell"><pre>llm openai endpoint http://127.0.0.1:9000/v1 <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>hello<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> -m gpt-5.4-mini</pre></div> <p>The bigger challenge with that kind of API concerns logging. If we're going to support the pattern where the message sequence is appended to on every request, ideally we can avoid logging all of that duplicate JSON for every turn.</p> <p>The solution is the new <a href="https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/logging.html#the-message-store">content-addressable message store</a>, modeled after Git. You can see the new schema for that <a href="https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/logging.html#sql-schema">in the documentation</a>, but the <code>llm logs</code> and <code>llm logs --json</code> commands have both been upgraded to convert that format back into something that's easy to consume.</p> <h4 id="and-the-rest">And the rest</h4> <p>There is a whole lot more in this release. The <a href="https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/changelog.html#v0-32">0.32 release notes</a> are pretty comprehensive, and the notes for <a href="https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/changelog.html#rc2-2026-07-30">0.32rc2</a>, <a href="https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/changelog.html#rc1-2026-07-30">0.32rc</a>, <a href="https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/changelog.html#a3-2026-06-09">0.32a3</a>, <a href="https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/changelog.html#a2-2026-05-12">0.32a2</a>, and <a href="https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/changelog.html#a0-2026-04-28">0.32a0</a> should fill in any gaps.</p> <p>Existing LLM plugins should all continue to work, but plugins that provide extra models will need to be upgraded to 0.32 in order to participate fully in the new streaming events system. There's a guide to implementing plugins with <a href="https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/plugins/advanced-model-plugins.html#structured-messages-and-streaming-events">Structured messages and streaming events</a> in the documentation.</p> <p>I've updated some of my own plugins:</p> <ul> <li> <a href="https://github.com/simonw/llm-anthropic/releases/tag/0.26">llm-anthropic 0.26</a> adds support for the Claude 5 family of models, plus <code>WebSearch</code>, <code>WebFetch</code>, <code>CodeExecution</code>, and <code>AnthropicMCP</code> server-side tools.</li> <li> <a href="https://github.com/simonw/llm-gemini">llm-gemini</a> and <a href="https://github.com/simonw/llm-openrouter">llm-openrouter</a> and <a href="https://github.com/simonw/llm-mistral">llm-mistral</a> are nearly there, releases coming soon.</li> </ul> <h4 id="i-guess-llm-is-an-agent-framework-now">I guess LLM is an agent framework now</h4> <p>Quite a few of the lower-level tools changes in this release were driven by the needs of <a href="https://agent.datasette.io/">Datasette Agent</a>. When I started work on LLM, the term "agent" had such a vague definition that I refused to use it. In <a href="https://simonwillison.net/2025/Sep/18/agents/">September 2025</a> I came around to the idea that "<strong>An LLM agent runs tools in a loop to achieve a goal</strong>" is well established enough now that I could stop avoiding the term entirely.</p> <p>Tool chains can now <a href="https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/python-api.html#python-api-tools-pause">pause for human approval</a> and <a href="https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/python-api.html#python-api-tools-resume">resume from a stored message history</a> - both needed by Datasette Agent.</p> <p>Looking at LLM today it's beginning to look very agent-shaped to me. There's something neat about having a CLI utility that can mix and match different tools from different sources with different models all as a one-liner, and that includes a Python library powerful enough to build systems like <a href="https://agent.datasette.io/">Datasette Agent</a> and <a href="https://github.com/simonw/llm-coding-agent">llm-coding-agent</a>.</p> <p>Maybe the next version of LLM will bake the concept of an "agent" into the core library. I'm still trying to figure out what that would look like.</p> <p>Tags: <a href="https://simonwillison.net/tags/projects">projects</a>, <a href="https://simonwillison.net/tags/releases">releases</a>, <a href="https://simonwillison.net/tags/ai">ai</a>, <a href="https://simonwillison.net/tags/openai">openai</a>, <a href="https://simonwillison.net/tags/generative-ai">generative-ai</a>, <a href="https://simonwillison.net/tags/llms">llms</a>, <a href="https://simonwillison.net/tags/llm">llm</a>, <a href="https://simonwillison.net/tags/anthropic">anthropic</a>, <a href="https://simonwillison.net/tags/llm-tool-use">llm-tool-use</a>, <a href="https://simonwillison.net/tags/llm-reasoning">llm-reasoning</a>, <a href="https://simonwillison.net/tags/model-context-protocol">model-context-protocol</a></p>

## [llm-anthropic 0.26](https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/4/llm-anthropic/#atom-everything)
*Simon Willison's Blog* | 04/08/2026 | Score: 1.00
Tags: mcp, product_launch, cli_tool, tool_update

> <p><strong>Release:</strong> <a href="https://github.com/simonw/llm-anthropic/releases/tag/0.26">llm-anthropic 0.26</a></p> <p>Includes new features enabled by <a href="https://simonwillison.net/2026/Aug/4/new-release-of-llm/">LLM 0.32</a>:</p> <blockquote> <ul> <li>New models: <code>claude-fable-5</code>, <code>claude-sonnet-5</code>, and <code>claude-opus-5</code>. <a href="https://github.com/simonw/llm-anthropic/issues/75">#75</a>, <a href="https://github.com/simonw/llm-anthropic/issues/76">#76</a></li> <li>Added server-side tools for <code>WebSearch</code>, <code>WebFetch</code>, <code>CodeExecution</code>, and <code>AnthropicMCP</code>, available through LLM's <code>-T</code> interface or Python <code>tools=</code>. The previous <code>-o web_search*</code> options have been removed in favor of <code>-T WebSearch</code>. <a href="https://github.com/simonw/llm-anthropic/issues/79">#79</a></li> <li>Upgraded to <a href="https://llm.datasette.io/en/stable/changelog.html#v0-32">llm>=0.32</a>. Reasoning, tool calls, tool results, and server-side tool results now stream as typed events. Reasoning for <code>llm</code> CLI prompts now displays to standard error unless you pass <code>--hide-reasoning/-R</code>.</li> <li>Simplified extended thinking to <code>thinking</code> and <code>thinking_effort</code> (<code>low</code>, <code>medium</code>, <code>high</code>, <code>xhigh</code>, or <code>max</code>). Claude 5 models think by default; <code>-o thinking 0</code> disables thinking for Sonnet 5 and Opus 5, while Fable 5 always thinks. <code>-R/--hide-reasoning</code> now omits reasoning from responses and logs. The <code>thinking_budget</code>, <code>thinking_display</code>, and <code>thinking_adaptive</code> options have been removed. <a href="https://github.com/simonw/llm-anthropic/issues/80">#80</a></li> </ul> </blockquote> <p>Tags: <a href="https://simonwillison.net/tags/llm">llm</a>, <a href="https://simonwillison.net/tags/anthropic">anthropic</a>, <a href="https://simonwillison.net/tags/claude">claude</a>, <a href="https://simonwillison.net/tags/model-context-protocol">model-context-protocol</a></p>

## [v0.16.0-dev.38: docs(scorecard): document eight Prisma compatibility gaps (#29881)](https://github.com/prisma/prisma/releases/tag/v0.16.0-dev.38)
*GitHub Releases · Prisma* | 04/08/2026 | Score: 1.00
Tags: api_update, cli_tool, tool_update

> <h2>Linked issue</h2> <p>n/a — small documentation change</p> <h2>At a glance</h2> <div class="highlight highlight-source-diff notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=" | `update` | ✅ | ✅ | — | ... | +| Empty-data `update` returns the matched row | ❌ | 🟡 | — | ... |"><pre> | `update` | ✅ | ✅ | — | ... | <span class="pl-mi1"><span class="pl-mi1">+</span>| Empty-data `update` returns the matched row | ❌ | 🟡 | — | ... |</span></pre></div> <p>Previously, broad green feature rows could hide narrower compatibility<br> gaps demonstrated by faithful Prisma functional-test ports.</p> <h2>Summary</h2> <p>This PR records eight known Prisma compatibility gaps as atomic<br> scorecard capabilities and links each unavailable verdict to its failing<br> integration-test evidence. It also recomputes the category and connector<br> totals so the scorecard index matches the underlying tables.</p> <h2>Decision</h2> <p>Represent each selected compatibility gap as its own feature row rather<br> than weakening broader rows for capabilities that otherwise work. A<br> connector with demonstrated failing coverage is marked <code>❌</code>; reachable<br> connectors without proving coverage remain <code>🟡</code>.</p> <h2>Reviewer notes</h2> <ul> <li>This is documentation-only; none of the eight underlying<br> implementation gaps are fixed here.</li> <li>The aggregate count changes include correction of a pre-existing<br> one-row discrepancy in the SQL ORM category declaration.</li> <li>The branch contains one signed-off commit and only scorecard files.</li> </ul> <h2>How it fits together</h2> <ol> <li>Add atomic rows for required Mongo composite validation, PostgreSQL<br> enum-array and generated-index emission, many-to-many relation counts,<br> JSON bytes serialization, bytes-key mutation reloads, multi-schema<br> relation filters, and empty updates.</li> <li>Link the unavailable verdicts to the faithful ports that demonstrate<br> each gap.</li> <li>Recompute the per-category row counts and all Postgres, SQLite, and<br> MongoDB verdict totals from the category tables.</li> </ol> <h2>Behavior changes &amp; evidence</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Known compatibility gaps are explicit rather than hidden by broad<br> feature verdicts.</strong> The rows land across<br> <a href="/prisma/prisma/blob/v0.16.0-dev.38/scorecard/02-types-and-values.md"><code>scorecard/02-types-and-values.md</code></a>,<br> <a href="/prisma/prisma/blob/v0.16.0-dev.38/scorecard/04-contract-emission-and-authoring.md"><code>scorecard/04-contract-emission-and-authoring.md</code></a>,<br> <a href="/prisma/prisma/blob/v0.16.0-dev.38/scorecard/06-sql-orm-client.md"><code>scorecard/06-sql-orm-client.md</code></a>,<br> <a href="/prisma/prisma/blob/v0.16.0-dev.38/scorecard/07-mongodb-query-and-orm.md"><code>scorecard/07-mongodb-query-and-orm.md</code></a>,<br> <a href="/prisma/prisma/blob/v0.16.0-dev.38/scorecard/08-relations.md"><code>scorecard/08-relations.md</code></a>, and<br> <a href="/prisma/prisma/blob/v0.16.0-dev.38/scorecard/11-aggregation-and-grouping.md"><code>scorecard/11-aggregation-and-grouping.md</code></a>,<br> with evidence from the corresponding integration ports.</li> <li><strong>The scorecard summary matches its category tables.</strong><br> <a href="/prisma/prisma/blob/v0.16.0-dev.38/scorecard.md"><code>scorecard.md</code></a> now reports 592 feature rows and 1,776<br> connector verdicts.</li> </ul> <h2>Testing performed</h2> <ul> <li>Mechanically counted every feature row and connector verdict across<br> <code>scorecard/*.md</code>; results match <code>scorecard.md</code>.</li> <li><code>git diff --check origin/main...HEAD</code></li> <li>No runtime tests run because the change is documentation-only.</li> </ul> <h2>Skill update</h2> <p>n/a — documentation-only scorecard update with no user-facing API or CLI<br> change</p> <h2>Alternatives considered</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Change the existing broad verdicts:</strong> rejected because capabilities<br> such as <code>update</code>, explicit many-to-many relations, and JSON values still<br> have passing integration coverage outside these narrower cases.</li> <li><strong>Maintain a separate known-issues list:</strong> rejected because atomic<br> scorecard rows keep each connector verdict and its evidence in the same<br> canonical matrix.</li> </ul> <h2>Checklist</h2> <ul class="contains-task-list"> <li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" id="" disabled="" class="task-list-item-checkbox" aria-label="Completed task" checked=""> All commits are signed off (<code>git commit -s</code>) per the<br> <a href="/prisma/prisma/blob/CONTRIBUTING.md#developer-certificate-of-origin-dco">DCO</a>.</li> <li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" id="" disabled="" class="task-list-item-checkbox" aria-label="Completed task" checked=""> I read <a href="/prisma/prisma/blob/CONTRIBUTING.md">CONTRIBUTING.md</a> and the change is<br> scoped to one logical concern.</li> <li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" id="" disabled="" class="task-list-item-checkbox" aria-label="Completed task" checked=""> Tests are updated (n/a — documentation-only change with no<br> behavioural delta).</li> <li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" id="" disabled="" class="task-list-item-checkbox" aria-label="Completed task" checked=""> The PR title follows the requested conventional documentation<br> format without a Linear prefix.</li> <li class="task-list-item"><input type="checkbox" id="" disabled="" class="task-list-item-checkbox" aria-label="Completed task" checked=""> The <strong>Skill update</strong> section above is filled in.</li> </ul> <h2>Summary by CodeRabbit</h2> <ul> <li><strong>Documentation</strong></li> <li>Expanded the feature scorecard with seven additional capability and<br> compatibility entries.</li> <li>Documented support status and test evidence for nested <code>Uint8Array</code><br> JSON values, enum-array constraints, generated index names, byte-key<br> mutations, MongoDB required-field writes, and cross-schema relations.</li> <li>Corrected the support status for relation-scoped many-to-many counts.</li> <li>Updated overall coverage totals and per-database support and<br> not-applicable counts.</li> </ul> <hr> <p>Signed-off-by: Steven McClankerton <a href="mailto:tatarintsev@prisma.io">tatarintsev@prisma.io</a><br> Co-authored-by: Steven McClankerton <a href="mailto:tatarintsev@prisma.io">tatarintsev@prisma.io</a></p>

Tags: developer_tool, cli_tool

> <h1>v0.17.0</h1> <p>This is the namespace release: Prisma Next now publishes as 17 packages under the <code>@prisma</code> scope, and an application depends on exactly one database facade. It also completes the structured error-code scheme across every plane, makes relation-loading lossless for big numbers and temporal values, and gives every SQL index and RLS policy an exact, migratable name.</p> <h2>Breaking changes</h2> <ul> <li> <p><strong>One <code>@prisma</code> package per application</strong> — the <code>@prisma-next/*</code> scope is retired; nothing publishes under it again. An application depends on exactly one database facade — <code>@prisma/orm-postgres</code>, <code>@prisma/orm-sqlite</code>, or <code>@prisma/orm-mongo</code> — plus any extension packs it uses (now named <code>@prisma/orm-extension-*</code>); everything else arrives as the facade's exact-pinned dependencies. Regenerating your contract rewrites generated imports to facade entrypoints with no <code>contractHash</code> change. See the <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma/blob/v0.17.0/skills/upgrade/prisma-next-upgrade/upgrades/0.16-to-0.17/">0.16-to-0.17 upgrade recipe</a> and the <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma/blob/v0.17.0/skills/extension-author/prisma-8-extension-upgrade/upgrades/0.16-to-0.17/">extension-author recipe</a>. (<a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma/pull/29864" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma/pull/29864/hovercard">#29864</a>, <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma/pull/29880" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma/pull/29880/hovercard">#29880</a>, <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma/pull/29883" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma/pull/29883/hovercard">#29883</a>, <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma/pull/29884" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma/pull/29884/hovercard">#29884</a>)</p> <p>Before:</p> <div class="highlight highlight-source-json-comments notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=""dependencies": { "@prisma-next/postgres": "0.16.0", "@prisma-next/framework-components": "0.16.0", "@prisma-next/sql-runtime": "0.16.0" }"><pre><span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>dependencies<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>: { <span class="pl-ent">"@prisma-next/postgres"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>0.16.0<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>, <span class="pl-ent">"@prisma-next/framework-components"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>0.16.0<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>, <span class="pl-ent">"@prisma-next/sql-runtime"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>0.16.0<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> }</pre></div> <p>After:</p> <div class="highlight highlight-source-json-comments notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content=""dependencies": { "@prisma/orm-postgres": "0.17.0" }"><pre><span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>dependencies<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>: { <span class="pl-ent">"@prisma/orm-postgres"</span>: <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>0.17.0<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> }</pre></div> </li> <li> <p><strong>Every published error is a structured envelope with a dotted code</strong> — the four legacy error systems (<code>PN-CLI-4001</code>-style codes, <code>RUNTIME.DECODE_FAILED</code>-style codes, and codeless error classes) consolidate into one scheme: a structural envelope carrying a <code>NAMESPACE.SUBCODE</code> code, recognized by the <code>isStructuredError</code> type predicate instead of <code>instanceof</code>. The ORM, contract-authoring, adapter/target, extension, and framework planes are all swept; legacy error classes (<code>PslFormatError</code>, the Supabase and SQL-escape classes, framework classes) are deleted. Prisma 7's <code>P1001</code>-style codes are not carried over. (<a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1016" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1016/hovercard">#1016</a>, <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1021" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1021/hovercard">#1021</a>, <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1025" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1025/hovercard">#1025</a>, <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1049" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1049/hovercard">#1049</a>, <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1053" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1053/hovercard">#1053</a>, <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1063" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1063/hovercard">#1063</a>)</p> <p>Before:</p> <div class="highlight highlight-source-ts notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="if (error instanceof PslFormatError) { report(error.diagnostics); }"><pre><span class="pl-k">if</span> <span class="pl-kos">(</span><span class="pl-s1">error</span> <span class="pl-k">instanceof</span> <span class="pl-v">PslFormatError</span><span class="pl-kos">)</span> <span class="pl-kos">{</span> <span class="pl-en">report</span><span class="pl-kos">(</span><span class="pl-s1">error</span><span class="pl-kos">.</span><span class="pl-c1">diagnostics</span><span class="pl-kos">)</span><span class="pl-kos">;</span> <span class="pl-kos">}</span></pre></div> <p>After:</p> <div class="highlight highlight-source-ts notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="if (isStructuredError(error) &amp;&amp; error.code === 'PSL.PARSE_FAILED') { report(error.meta.diagnostics); }"><pre><span class="pl-k">if</span> <span class="pl-kos">(</span><span class="pl-en">isStructuredError</span><span class="pl-kos">(</span><span class="pl-s1">error</span><span class="pl-kos">)</span> <span class="pl-c1">&amp;&amp;</span> <span class="pl-s1">error</span><span class="pl-kos">.</span><span class="pl-c1">code</span> <span class="pl-c1">===</span> <span class="pl-s">'PSL.PARSE_FAILED'</span><span class="pl-kos">)</span> <span class="pl-kos">{</span> <span class="pl-en">report</span><span class="pl-kos">(</span><span class="pl-s1">error</span><span class="pl-kos">.</span><span class="pl-c1">meta</span><span class="pl-kos">.</span><span class="pl-c1">diagnostics</span><span class="pl-kos">)</span><span class="pl-kos">;</span> <span class="pl-kos">}</span></pre></div> </li> <li> <p><strong>Content hashes are bare hex</strong> — the <code>sha256:</code> prefix is gone from every surface (emitted contracts, migration manifests, refs, CLI output, and the database marker), and loaders reject the prefixed form. Contract hash values are unchanged; <code>migrationHash</code> values change. A codemod in the <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma/blob/v0.17.0/skills/upgrade/prisma-next-upgrade/upgrades/0.16-to-0.17/">0.16-to-0.17 recipe</a> converts checked-in migration trees. (<a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1033" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1033/hovercard">#1033</a>)</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Migration contract snapshots move into a content-addressed store</strong> — per-migration sibling snapshot files and ref-paired copies are replaced by a single <code>migrations/snapshots/<hex>/</code> store per migrations root; every distinct contract is stored once, and <code>migration.ts</code> imports its bookend contracts from the store. This is a clean break with no fallback reader; a one-shot migrator (<code>scripts/migrate-migrations-layout.mjs</code>) converts existing trees and re-verifies every <code>migrationHash</code> unchanged. (<a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1018" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1018/hovercard">#1018</a>, <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1024" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1024/hovercard">#1024</a>)</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>PostgreSQL native types are authored in type position; the <code>@db.*</code> attribute channel is removed</strong> — write the native type directly (<code>VarChar(255)</code>, <code>Uuid</code>, <code>Timestamptz</code>) instead of a base type plus <code>@db.*</code> attribute; remaining <code>@db.X(args)</code> usage fails with the exact replacement spelled out. <code>Json</code> re-binds to native <code>json</code> storage, with a new <code>Jsonb</code> scalar for jsonb (what every pre-0.16 <code>Json</code> field meant — switch those fields to keep a byte-identical contract), and <code>Date</code> re-binds to the correct <code>pg/date@1</code> codec. (<a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1022" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1022/hovercard">#1022</a>, <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1036" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1036/hovercard">#1036</a>, <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1054" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1054/hovercard">#1054</a>)</p> <p>Before:</p> <div class="highlight highlight-source-prisma notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="model User { id String @id @db.Uuid name String @db.VarChar(255) }"><pre><span class="pl-s1"><span class="pl-k">model</span> <span class="pl-en">User</span> {</span> <span class="pl-s1"> <span class="pl-smi">id</span> <span class="pl-c1">String</span> <span class="pl-s1"><span class="pl-en">@id</span></span> <span class="pl-s1"><span class="pl-en">@db.Uuid</span></span></span> <span class="pl-s1"> <span class="pl-smi">name</span> <span class="pl-c1">String</span> <span class="pl-s1"><span class="pl-en">@db.VarChar</span>(<span class="pl-c1">255</span>)</span></span> <span class="pl-s1">}</span></pre></div> <p>After:</p> <div class="highlight highlight-source-prisma notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="model User { id Uuid @id name VarChar(255) }"><pre><span class="pl-s1"><span class="pl-k">model</span> <span class="pl-en">User</span> {</span> <span class="pl-s1"> <span class="pl-smi">id</span> <span class="pl-c1">Uuid</span> <span class="pl-s1"><span class="pl-en">@id</span></span></span> <span class="pl-s1"> <span class="pl-smi">name</span> <span class="pl-c1">VarChar</span>(255)</span> <span class="pl-s1">}</span></pre></div> </li> <li> <p><strong>Relation-loading and aggregates are lossless</strong> — values read through <code>.include()</code> no longer pass through lossy JSON: every codec gains an explicit lossless JSON form produced inside the database. 64-bit integers arrive as <code>bigint</code> instead of silently rounding, decimals as exact strings, and temporal columns decode correctly. Aggregate result types change accordingly: <code>count()</code> is a <code>bigint</code>, decimal sums are strings. Regenerate your contract after upgrading. (<a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma/pull/29844" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma/pull/29844/hovercard">#29844</a>, <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1023" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1023/hovercard">#1023</a>, <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1051" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1051/hovercard">#1051</a>)</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>SQL indexes and RLS policies are name-identified</strong> — every index and RLS policy carries an exact name in the contract, names travel on the wire, live objects can be adopted by exact name (<code>@@map</code>), and a rename converges by renaming instead of drop-and-recreate. (<a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1047" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1047/hovercard">#1047</a>, <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma/pull/29807" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma/pull/29807/hovercard">#29807</a>, <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma/pull/29865" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma/pull/29865/hovercard">#29865</a>)</p> </li> <li> <p><strong><code>extensionPacks</code> config key renamed to <code>extensions</code></strong> — in <code>prisma-next.config.ts</code>, the TS builder, client options, and the emitted contract's top-level key. The old key fails loudly. Because the key sits in the hashed contract bytes, all contract hashes change: re-emit and re-anchor migrations per the recipe. Two smaller key renames ride along: <code>contract.source.sourceFormat</code> → <code>format</code>, and the facade <code>defineConfig</code> option <code>outputPath</code> → <code>output</code>. (<a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1032" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1032/hovercard">#1032</a>)</p> </li> <li> <p><strong>Count-only mutation terminals renamed</strong> — <code>createCount(...)</code> / <code>updateCount(...)</code> / <code>deleteCount()</code> become <code>createAndCount(...)</code> / <code>updateAndCount(...)</code> / <code>deleteAndCount()</code>; behavior and <code>Promise<number></code> results are unchanged, with no compatibility aliases. (<a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1044" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1044/hovercard">#1044</a>)</p> </li> </ul> <h2>Features</h2> <ul> <li>Expression, partial, and unique indexes are authorable in both PSL and the TypeScript builder. (<a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1048" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1048/hovercard">#1048</a>)</li> <li><code>contract infer</code> reaches full fidelity — indexes, policy blocks, and <code>@@rls</code> are captured — and signs the database, so introspect-then-verify works end to end on an adopted database. It also infers 1:1 relations from unique indexes. (<a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma/pull/29808" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma/pull/29808/hovercard">#29808</a>, <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1038" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1038/hovercard">#1038</a>)</li> <li>Every error code is documented on an in-repo reference page (221 codes), kept complete by a CI check, and error envelopes carry a <code>docsUrl</code> pointing at their per-code anchor. (<a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1027" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1027/hovercard">#1027</a>, <a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma/pull/29806" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma/pull/29806/hovercard">#29806</a>)</li> </ul> <h2>Fixes</h2> <ul> <li>MongoDB write results decode through their type codecs instead of returning raw wire values. (<a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma/pull/29879" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma/pull/29879/hovercard">#29879</a>)</li> <li>The Postgres runtime driver serializes queries per pinned client, fixing interleaved-query failures on a shared connection. (<a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma/pull/29839" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma/pull/29839/hovercard">#29839</a>)</li> <li>Mixed-case native-enum casts are quoted, so PascalCase enum type names survive Postgres case-folding. (<a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1034" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1034/hovercard">#1034</a>)</li> <li>Driver cursor streaming runs inside an explicit transaction, fixing dropped-portal failures under load. (<a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1017" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma-next/pull/1017/hovercard">#1017</a>)</li> <li>Published type declarations name only dependencies a consumer will actually have installed. (<a href="https://github.com/prisma/prisma/pull/29862" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/prisma/prisma/pull/29862/hovercard">#29862</a>)</li> </ul>
